newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican protesters denounce Fujimori for assault.
newsitem.headline: Mexican protesters denounce Fujimori for assault.

text.p: Demonstrators hurled red paint and tomatoes at the Peruvian embassy in Mexico City on Wednesday in protest of Peru's bloody assault to end the hostage saga at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
About 50 protesters, most belonging to the leftist Assembly of Neighbourhoods group, shouted "Fujimori murderer" and "Latin America is in mourning."

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori on Tuesday ended the 126-day saga by ordering a military assault on the diplomatic site, which was seized by Peru's leftist Tupac Amaru guerrillas during a party on Dec. 17.
All 14 rebels, one of the 72 hostages and two soldiers died in the assault.
In Mexico City, 14 candles were placed at the front of the embassy, one for each fallen rebel. One protester held up a picture of Fujimori labeled "Hitlermori."
Among those protesters in Mexico City was Superbarrio, a "social fighter" famous for his cowl and costume that is half-super hero, half-professional wrestler.
Three unarmed guards watched as the protesters soiled the embassy grounds with paint.
